target.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nothing limits how often recurring cron jobs can fire. An agent (or CLI caller) can schedule a `30s` job that runs an LLM turn forever — on hosted/operator deployments that is unbounded spend with no operator control. Cron has a concurrency guardrail (`cron.maxConcurrentRuns`) but no cadence guardrail. Related: #76473 explores a warning-only variant; this PR is the enforceable operator limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

One opt-in config value, `cron.minInterval`, enforced in two layers:

1. **Creation/edit rejection (UX layer):** `create`, schedule-changing `update`, and declaration-keyed `add` converges of a recurring `every`/`cron` job below the floor fail with a clear error (`cron schedule fires every 30s, below the minimum interval of 5m`; gateway maps it to `INVALID_REQUEST`). The cron tool description tells agents to increase the interval instead of retrying. For `cron` expressions this samples upcoming fires — documented as best-effort, since bounded sampling cannot prove an expression's true minimum gap.
2. **Fire-time floor (enforcement layer):** the scheduler paces every `nextRunAtMs` re-arm so consecutive fires of a recurring job stay at least `minInterval` apart (start-to-start, launchd `ThrottleInterval`-style). This is the contract the docs promise: it covers jobs created before the limit was configured, expressions whose tight gaps escape sampling, restarts/missed-slot catch-up, error-backoff retries, update re-arms, and maintenance recomputes. Deferred fires log a warning naming the job.

Scope decisions: one-shot `at` jobs are exempt; forced manual runs never shift the schedule and are not floored; transient-failure retries still follow `cron.retry` but recurring re-fires are lower-bounded by the floor; a 2s dispatch slack (clamped to half the floor) keeps schedules whose cadence exactly equals the floor on their natural slots — no drift, no warning spam.

## User Impact

None by default: unset/`0` means no limit and preserves shipped behavior exactly. With the limit set:

```json5
{
  cron: {
    minInterval: "5m", // duration string ("30s", "5m", "1h") or milliseconds
  },
}
```

recurring jobs neither validate nor fire more often than every 5 minutes. Config surface: `CronConfig.minInterval` + zod schema with duration validation, help text, label, and docs (`docs/automation/cron-jobs.md`, `docs/cli/cron.md`, configuration reference).

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. The rebase re-ported validation and the floor onto main's refactored update path (`updateLoadedJob`/`finalizeUpdatedJob`), and extended creation-time validation to the declarative `add()` converge path — post-refactor, an `add` with a `declarationKey` could otherwise change an existing job's schedule without hitting the floor check.

- Post-rebase, all green (4 Vitest shards): full cron subsystem (`src/cron`, 100+ test files), `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts`, `src/config/cron-limits.test.ts`, `src/config/zod-schema.cron-min-interval.test.ts`, `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts`, `test/scripts/prompt-snapshots.test.ts`.
- Behavior tests (`src/cron/service.min-interval-floor.test.ts`, `src/cron/service/jobs.min-interval.test.ts`, extended `timer.regression`): pre-existing every/cron jobs paced + warned; error-path pacing; no-floor regression guard; at-floor cadence stays on natural slots under dispatch jitter; force runs preserve the schedule; enable-toggle update keeps the floor; startup catch-up does not replay a missed slot inside the floor window.
- `tsgo` core/test lanes clean for touched code; prompt snapshots regenerated via `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`.
- Multi-agent adversarial review of the floor ran pre-push; every confirmed finding (force-run schedule shift, enable-toggle bypass, restart catch-up/backoff bypasses, at-floor jitter drift, maintenance repair undoing deferrals) is fixed and regression-tested above.

target.title: feat(message): add universal pagination contract with cursor support for MSTeams
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses #71452 — provides the shared pagination contract and CLI cursor support, and wires MSTeams search, list-pins, and channel-list as the first provider implementation.

Previously, `renderPaginationHint` inspected provider-specific raw payload fields (`hasMore`, `nextBatch`, `@odata.nextLink`, `total_results`) with no shared contract. Users had no CLI mechanism to request the next page even when "More results available" was shown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduces a universal cursor-based pagination model across the shared runner, formatter, and CLI layers, replacing ad-hoc per-provider field inspection with a single `MessageActionPagination` type. Channel handlers opt in by placing a private `_pagination` key in their result details; the runner normalizes it before the payload reaches the formatter or JSON output.

### Architecture

```
CLI --cursor <token>  ->  params.cursor  ->  plugin handler  ->  API
                                                                |
                       result.details._pagination        <------+
                                                                |
                       extractPagination(handled)          ->  result.pagination
                                                                |
                       renderPaginationHint(result.pagination)  ->  "More results. Use --cursor ..."
                       buildMessageCliJson(result)              ->  { pagination: { hasMore, nextCursor } }
```

### Key decisions

- **Opaque `nextCursor` string**: channels produce whatever token their API uses (offset number, nextLink URL, batch token). The CLI and formatter never parse it.
- **Private `_pagination` key**: zero SDK changes. Channels opt in voluntarily. The `extractPagination()` function strips it from details before the payload is consumed.
- **After-extract-delete semantics**: `extractPagination` runs before `extractToolPayload`, so end-user payload is clean.
- **`--cursor` CLI flag** on `read`, `pins`, `search` — the three list-producing actions.
- **Cursor URL validation**: `searchMessagesMSTeams` validates cursor URLs against known Microsoft Graph API origins (`v1.0`, `beta`) before forwarding auth headers.
- **Legacy fallback**: `renderPayloadPaginationHint` preserves existing payload-based hints for providers not yet migrated to `MessageActionPagination`.

## User Impact

**MSTeams users** can now paginate search results, pin lists, and channel lists.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve fresh tool results during aggregate recovery
target.body:
Fixes #99481
Related: #96857, #98955

## Summary

Preserve the current fresh tool-result text during prompt-history aggregate recovery when the fresh result is followed by a runtime/context message before provider dispatch.

## Breaking changes

None.

## What Problem This Solves

#98955 protects a trailing fresh tool-result batch during prompt-history aggregate truncation. #99481 showed the empty tool-result symptom could still happen on `2026.7.1-beta.1`, where that trailing protection was already present.

The remaining gap is non-trailing fresh tool results: runtime/context messages can be inserted after a fresh result before the provider call. The existing trailing-only scan then does not mark that fresh result as protected, so a saturated long-lived session can spend aggregate recovery on the current result and leave the model blind to the latest tool output.

## Implementation

- Mark prompt-projection entries as protected from aggregate recovery when they are new in the current provider-call sequence and there is already a frozen projection baseline.
- Keep the first provider call free to trim historical saturated tool output by only applying the new projection protection after projection state has frozen at least one prior call.
- Keep the existing trailing-batch protection intact as a separate protection source.
- Use older unprotected projected history first, then ineligible older history when protected output exists, and only allow non-trailing fresh projection entries as last-resort recovery candidates.
- Add regression coverage where saturated history is followed by a fresh `exec`-style tool result and then a runtime-context-like message.

## Labels considered

- `agents`
- `size: S`
- `P1`
- `proof: sufficient`
- `merge-risk: 🚨 session-state`
- `status: 👀 ready for maintainer look`

## Validation

- Current PR head: `99aee9a7a6b4c2c946b1e2a257cf8be40aa509ae`.
- Merge state after rebasing on latest `main`: `MERGEABLE` / `CLEAN`.
- Local pre-check on the current head:
  - `git diff --check -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` passed.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` passed: 1 file, 58 tests.
- GitHub Actions on the current head:
  - Latest PR check table: 66 success / 29 skipped / 1 neutral / 0 failure / 0 pending.
  - CI run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28787583708.
  - `checks-node-compact-large-whole-1` included `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` with 58 tests passing.
  - Real behavior proof, OpenGrep PR diff, Workflow Sanity, Dependency Guard, Security Sensitive Guard, CodeQL, and CodeQL Critical Quality completed without failures on the same head.

## Evidence source map

- Reported shipped symptom: #99481 reports empty tool-result delivery on `2026.7.1-beta.1`, after the trailing-result protection from #98955 was already present.
- Related broader class: #96857 tracks the broader model-visible tool-result text loss/degradation class.
- Root-cause coverage: the new regression constructs saturated projected history, adds a fresh `fresh_exec` tool result, then appends a runtime-context-like message so trailing-only protection no longer applies.
- After-fix behavior covered by tests:
  - the fresh visible text remains `"ABC"`;
  - aggregate recovery engages;
  - aggregate tool-result text stays within the configured `32_000` character budget;
  - older historical tool results are reduced;
  - trailing protected batches and persisted protected trailing batches keep their existing intact behavior.

## Risk

Low to moderate. The changed surface is the provider prompt-projection truncation/recovery path for saturated sessions. The tradeoff is intentional: when current fresh tool output and older projected history cannot both fit, recovery spends budget on older history before the current fresh result.

Compatibility risk is bounded by keeping trailing-batch protection and persisted trailing-batch behavior separate from the new non-trailing fresh-projection protection. Oversized fresh results still go through the per-result cap, and non-trailing protected fresh projection entries are only last-resort aggregate candidates after older candidates cannot recover enough budget.

## Rollback

Revert this PR to restore the previous aggregate recovery ordering. No data migration or config rollback is required.

## Docs updated

No docs change. This is an internal prompt-projection recovery fix; regression tests document the behavior boundary.

## Related issue / PR

- Fixes #99481
- Related: #96857
- Related prior fix: #98955

## Not tested / Limitations

- No transport-specific saturated-session WebChat, Discord, or Telegram run was added in this PR. Coverage is at the prompt-projection helper level plus the current GitHub Actions CI matrix for the touched agent surface.

## Review context addressed

- Resolved the merge conflict with latest `main`.
- Preserved the existing trailing-batch and persisted trailing-batch protection behavior while adding the runtime-context-following fresh-result path.
- Strengthened current-head validation and replaced older head evidence with current head `99aee9a7a6b4c2c946b1e2a257cf8be40aa509ae`.

## Maintainer / ClawSweeper review addressed

- ClawSweeper noted that this PR changes which tool-result text survives under saturated aggregate recovery. The PR now states the intended tradeoff explicitly and keeps trailing protected batches separate from non-trailing fresh projection entries.
- ClawSweeper noted that earlier proof was helper-level rather than a full transport run. The limitation remains documented, and the current head has focused helper coverage plus green GitHub Actions for the touched agent shard and broader CI checks.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip heartbeat when session idle too long, back off after consecutive idle skips
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Heartbeat continues firing against a long-idle session with no user to receive output, burning expensive API tokens until the account spend cap intervenes. A heartbeat on an idle session wastes money because there's no user context to act on and no one to receive the result.

- **Problem**: `runHeartbeatOnce()` has no awareness of session staleness. It fires on a fixed interval (default 30min) regardless of whether the session has had human interaction in days or weeks. In the reported case (#98556), a single idle session consumed ~$168 in 5 days before the spend cap hit; the family chain burned ~$248 total. Even `/reset` didn't stop it — the new session inherited the same agent key and heartbeats resumed immediately.
- **Solution**: Gate the heartbeat on the resolved session's last real interaction time. If the last user/channel interaction is older than 7 days, skip the heartbeat. Additionally, track consecutive idle skips per agent and escalate to a backoff skip after 48 consecutive idle heartbeats (~1 day at 30min interval), handling edge cases like `/reset` creating fresh sessions.
- **What changed**: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` (~40 lines of runtime logic), `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.test-utils.ts` (extended `HeartbeatSessionSeed` type), new `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.idle-gate.test.ts` (7 test cases).
- **What did NOT change**: No new config keys, types, schema, or public API. No changes to `heartbeat-wake.ts`, `heartbeat-schedule.ts`, or the scheduler layer. No behavioral change for active sessions.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #98556
- Related to #14051
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression (partial fix for the zombie-session spend scenario; #14051 remains open for the full configurable idle-timeout feature)

## Motivation

Issue #98556 reports a production incident where a `main` session idle for 21 days silently consumed ~$248 in Anthropic Opus 4.7 spend through heartbeat polls that fired every 30 minutes. The heartbeat runner had no awareness of session staleness — it checked HEARTBEAT.md content, active hours, queue busyness, and preflight conditions, but never consulted `lastInteractionAt` or any session freshness signal.

This is a runtime safety guard, not a product feature. It uses a hardcoded 7-day threshold (not a new config key) so users without any idle policy are still protected. Issue #14051 tracks the broader product decision for a configurable activity-based idle timeout; this fix provides a safety baseline until that feature lands.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Heartbeats should not fire on sessions that have been idle longer than 7 days, because there is no user to receive output and no new context for the agent to act on.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 22, branch `fix/heartbeat-idle-gate-98556`, based on `origin/main` HEAD.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  1. Ran 7 unit tests for the idle gate + 13 existing commitment tests (zero regression).
  2. Ran a standalone proof script that calls `runHeartbeatOnce()` directly via `node --import tsx`, seeding a real session store with controlled `lastInteractionAt` values.

- **Evidence after fix**:

  ```console
  $ node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-98556-evidence/proof.mts

  === Heartbeat Idle Gate: Real Runtime Proof ===

  [1/3] Active session (1 min idle)
        status: ran

  [2/3] Idle session (8 days idle)
        status: skipped, reason: session-idle

  [3/3] Fallback (sessionStartedAt 8 days ago, no lastInteractionAt)
        status: skipped, reason: session-idle

  === All tests passed ===
  ```

  | Test case | Input | Expected | Result |
  |-----------|-------|----------|--------|
  | Active session | `lastInteractionAt = 1 min ago` | `status: "ran"` | ✅ `ran` |
  | Idle 8 days | `lastInteractionAt = 8 days ago` | `status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle"` | ✅ `skipped / session-idle` |
  | No lastInteractionAt | `sessionStartedAt = 8 days ago` | `status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle"` | ✅ `skipped / session-idle` |
  | Unit: exactly at threshold | `lastInteractionAt = 7d+1ms ago` | skip | ✅ |
  | Unit: only updatedAt | `updatedAt = 7d+1m ago` | skip | ✅ |
  | Unit: recent sessionStartedAt | `sessionStartedAt = 1 min ago` | ran | ✅ |
  | Unit: no entry | no seed data | ran (no-op) | ✅ |

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. Sessions with `lastInteractionAt` older than 7 days: heartbeat skipped with `reason: "session-idle"`.
  2. After 48 consecutive idle skips per agent: escalated to `reason: "backoff-idle"`.
  3. Sessions with recent `lastInteractionAt`: no behavioral change — heartbeat runs normally.
  4. Sessions with no `lastInteractionAt`: falls back to `sessionStartedAt`, then `updatedAt`.
  5. Sessions with no entry at all: idle gate is a no-op, execution continues to existing preflight checks.
- **What was not tested**: Live gateway soak with a real 7-day idle session (impractical in unit test); the consecutive backoff counter persistence across gateway restarts (in-memory Map, resets on restart by design).

## Root Cause

The heartbeat runner (`runHeartbeatOnce()` in `heartbeat-runner.ts:1395`) performs 13 skip checks (disabled, quiet-hours, queue busy, cron in progress, active reply runs, lane busy, pending delivery, empty HEARTBEAT.md, etc.) but never consults the resolved session's interaction staleness. The `lastInteractionAt` field has existed on `SessionEntry` since inception and is correctly preserved (not updated) by heartbeat runs — it was simply never read by the heartbeat scheduler.

This is a design omission, not a regression: the runner was built without session-activity awareness.

```
Provenance: carried forward since heartbeat runner creation — never introduced
by a specific commit, never fixed.
Confidence: clear
```

## Regression Test Plan

7 new unit tests cover the idle gate behavior. 13 existing commitment tests confirm zero regression. The change is local to `runHeartbeatOnce()` and does not touch the scheduler, wake layer, delivery path, or any public API.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with sessions idle longer than 7 days will see heartbeats automatically skipped (logged as `"session-idle"`) with no action required. Active sessions are unaffected. No new configuration or user intervention needed.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Reproduction + Verification

### Environment (unit test)
- OS: Linux x86_64
- Runtime/container: Node.js 22

### Steps (unit test)
1. Seed session store with `lastInteractionAt` set to more than 7 days ago.
2. Call `runHeartbeatOnce()` with `target: "none"`.
3. Observe `{ status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle" }`.

### Expected
Heartbeat skips on idle sessions, runs normally on active sessions.

### Actual (before fix)
Heartbeat runs regardless of session staleness.

## Evidence Checklist

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets (unit test output)
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: 7 test cases covering idle/active/no-entry/fallback chains; 13 existing commitment tests for regression.
- **Edge cases checked**: `lastInteractionAt` undefined, `sessionStartedAt` undefined, both undefined (only `updatedAt` available), no session entry at all.
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live gateway with real 7-day idle session (logistically impractical); the consecutive backoff counter persisting across gateway restarts (by design it's an in-memory Map).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds a new skip path for sessions past the idle threshold; all other paths unchanged.
- [x] Config/env changes? No — no new config keys, env vars, or schema changes.
- [x] Migration needed? No.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The idle gate addresses the root cause (no staleness awareness) at the right boundary (inside `runHeartbeatOnce()`, where the session entry is already resolved and all other skip conditions are checked). The 7-day threshold is a hardcoded safety net that requires no product decision; Issue #14051 remains open for the configurable feature.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**:
  1. Adding a new config key `heartbeat.idleTimeoutMinutes` — rejected because CLAUDE.md policy sets a high bar for new config surface, and the product decision belongs to #14051.
  2. Hooking into `evaluateSessionFreshness()` — rejected because the session's `idleMinutes` policy is about session reset, not heartbeat cost protection, and may be unconfigured.
  3. Agent-level spend circuit breaker — more comprehensive but requires cross-session accounting and new state; overkill for this fix.

## Relationship to #14051

Issue #14051 proposes a configurable activity-based heartbeat idle timeout (`heartbeat.idleTimeoutMinutes`). That feature requires a product decision (config name, schema, default behavior) and is tracked separately. This PR does **not** implement #14051. Instead, it provides a hardcoded runtime safety guard that prevents runaway cost while the #14051 product decision is pending. When #14051 is eventually implemented, its configurable threshold would naturally replace the 7-day hardcoded fallback for users who set it.

ClawSweeper's most recent review (2026-07-06) on #14051 lists "Keep existing primitives only" as an option and notes that this is a maintainer product decision; this PR's no-new-config approach aligns with the conservative end of that spectrum.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Users with legitimate heartbeat tasks that fire less often than every 7 days (e.g., a weekly heartbeat report).  
**Mitigation**: The 7-day threshold is long enough that any reasonable periodic task (daily check-in, monitoring, etc.) will fire well within the window. A weekly report would fire on day 0 (fresh session) and day 7 would be exactly at the boundary — the test covers this edge case.  
**Compatibility impact**: None for active sessions. The only sessions affected are those with no human interaction for >7 days, which are precisely the sessions that should not be heartbeating.  
**Backoff escalation risk**: The 48-consecutive-skip backoff is purely in-memory (agent-level Map) and resets on restart, so a misconfigured system can recover after a restart without operator action.

---

AI-assisted: Yes
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Human confirmed understanding of code changes: Yes

Related to #98556
Related to #14051

target.title: fix(agents): suppress unhandled stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox SSH commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runSshCommand` and the tar-over-SSH pipe transfer in sandbox/ssh.ts attach `data` listeners to child process stdout/stderr streams, but do not attach `error` listeners. If any stream emits an `error` event, the unhandled error can crash the OpenClaw process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add no-op `error` handlers to all child stdout/stderr streams that have data listeners. Stream read errors are treated as non-fatal because the child process `error`/`close` handlers already report the real outcome.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts`** — add `child.stdout.on("error", () => {})` and `child.stderr.on("error", () => {})` in `runSshCommand` (2 lines) + `tar.stderr`/`ssh.stdout`/`ssh.stderr` error handlers in the pipe transfer path (3 lines)

## Evidence

```bash
node --import tsx/esm scripts/proof/ssh-stream-errors.mts
```

```
==============================================================
Proof: stream error handlers in sandbox/ssh.ts
==============================================================
```

target.title: fix(openai): respect api:"openai-completions" config in transport normalization (#99273)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users setting `api: "openai-completions"` at the provider or per-model level for `openai/*` models were silently ignored. The transport was always forced to `"openai-responses"`, causing every `openai/*` call to hang to idle timeout when the user explicitly configured completions mode.

Fixes #99273.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original fix was a single-character change (`!==` → `===`) in `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`. However, that same predicate is also used by `normalizeOpenAITransport` to convert catalog-default `"openai-completions"` rows to the current Responses API for native OpenAI models. A simple swap would stop catalog normalization and regress the live test.

The fix now has three coordinated parts:

1. **`shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport`** (L462): `!==` → `===`. When the caller explicitly requested completions, return false (don't force Responses). This guard fires at transport time only.

2. **`normalizeOpenAITransport`** (L480-501): Replaced the `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport` call with direct catalog-default checks (isOwnerProvider + isOpenAIBaseUrl + api is completions or absent). This preserves catalog-to-Responses normalization independently.

3. **`normalizeResolvedModel` and `normalizeTransport` callbacks**: Check `ctx.config.models.providers.openai.api` before normalizing. When the user explicitly set provider-level `api`, the callbacks skip the transformation so the user's intent is preserved through both resolution and transport.

**Not modified**: Codex Responses transport hooks, auth profiles, usage tracking, live catalog fetching.

## User Impact

Users who explicitly configure `api: "openai-completions"` for OpenAI models now have their configuration respected. Default behavior for catalog OpenAI models (normalize to Responses) is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: `api: "openai-completions"` config is ignored for `openai/*` models at provider and per-model level.

**Real environment tested**: Local vitest, no external credentials required.

**Evidence after fix**:

All 4 scenarios verified at both resolution and transport time:

| Scenario | normalizeResolvedModel | normalizeTransport | Expected |
|----------|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Catalog model, no user config | → `openai-responses` ✅ | exposes Responses ✅ | Catalog defaults preserved |
| Explicit provider `api: "openai-completions"` | → stays `openai-completions` ✅ | returns `undefined` ✅ | User config respected |
| Transport with catalog default | — | → `{api:"openai-responses"}` ✅ | Transport normalizes |
| Transport with explicit config | — | → `undefined` ✅ | No override |

--- [BEFORE fix] ---
```
shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport(api="openai-completions")
  ai !== "openai-completions" → false → continues → checks provider=openai
    → baseUrl=default → returns TRUE → FORCES Responses
  ❌ User's explicit completions config silently rewritten to Responses
```

--- [AFTER fix] ---
```
normalizeResolvedModel callback:
  ctx.config.models.providers.openai.api === "openai-completions"?
  → YES → return ctx.model unchanged ✅
normalizeTransport callback:
  ctx.config.models.providers.openai.api === "openai-completions"?
  → YES → return undefined (no override) ✅
```

**Observed result after fix**: Explicit `api: "openai-completions"` survives both resolution and transport normalization. Catalog models continue to normalize to Responses as before.

## Regression Test Plan

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts
→ exit 0
```

## Root Cause

In `shouldUseOpenAIResponsesTransport` (`extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts:462`), `!==` was used instead of `===` when checking for `"openai-completions"`. The condition was intended to short-circuit when the user explicitly requested completions mode, but the inverted operator caused completions to fall through to the default responses path.

Additionally, the same function was shared by `normalizeOpenAITransport` (catalog normalization) and `normalizeTransport` (transport-time override), creating a coupling that made the one-character fix insufficient: the catalog path also needed the predicate to return false for `"openai-completions"` models. The fix decouples the two paths so each has its own correct logic.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Model used**: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)

target.title: feat(message): add universal pagination contract with cursor support for MSTeams
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses #71452 — provides the shared pagination contract and CLI cursor support, and wires MSTeams search, list-pins, and channel-list as the first provider implementation.

Previously, `renderPaginationHint` inspected provider-specific raw payload fields (`hasMore`, `nextBatch`, `@odata.nextLink`, `total_results`) with no shared contract. Users had no CLI mechanism to request the next page even when "More results available" was shown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduces a universal cursor-based pagination model across the shared runner, formatter, and CLI layers, replacing ad-hoc per-provider field inspection with a single `MessageActionPagination` type. Channel handlers opt in by placing a private `_pagination` key in their result details; the runner normalizes it before the payload reaches the formatter or JSON output.

### Architecture

```
CLI --cursor <token>  ->  params.cursor  ->  plugin handler  ->  API
                                                                |
                       result.details._pagination        <------+
                                                                |
                       extractPagination(handled)          ->  result.pagination
                                                                |
                       renderPaginationHint(result.pagination)  ->  "More results. Use --cursor ..."
                       buildMessageCliJson(result)              ->  { pagination: { hasMore, nextCursor } }
```

### Key decisions

- **Opaque `nextCursor` string**: channels produce whatever token their API uses (offset number, nextLink URL, batch token). The CLI and formatter never parse it.
- **Private `_pagination` key**: zero SDK changes. Channels opt in voluntarily. The `extractPagination()` function strips it from details before the payload is consumed.
- **After-extract-delete semantics**: `extractPagination` runs before `extractToolPayload`, so end-user payload is clean.
- **`--cursor` CLI flag** on `read`, `pins`, `search` — the three list-producing actions.
- **Cursor URL validation**: `searchMessagesMSTeams` validates cursor URLs against known Microsoft Graph API origins (`v1.0`, `beta`) before forwarding auth headers.
- **Legacy fallback**: `renderPayloadPaginationHint` preserves existing payload-based hints for providers not yet migrated to `MessageActionPagination`.

## User Impact

**MSTeams users** can now paginate search results, pin lists, and channel lists.

**Other channels** (Discord, Slack, Matrix, Feishu) continue to work unchanged via the legacy fallback and will get pagination in follow-up PRs using the same contract.

## Evidence

### Real CLI output (production `formatMessageCliText` code path)

**Step 1 — first page:**

```
$ openclaw message search "deploy" --channel msteams --target "19:abc@thread.tacv2" --limit 5

Search results
| Time                 | Author   | Text                                            | Id       |
|----------------------|----------|-------------------------------------------------|----------|
| 2026-07-01T10:00:00Z | alice    | deploy v2.3.1 to production                     | msg-0    |
| 2026-07-01T10:05:00Z | bob      | deploy failed: port conflict                    | msg-1    |
| 2026-07-01T10:08:00Z | alice    | deploy retry with --force                       | msg-2    |
| 2026-07-01T10:12:00Z | ci-bot   | deploy v2.3.1 succeeded                         | msg-3    |
| 2026-07-02T09:00:00Z | charlie  | deploy v2.3.2 scheduled                         | msg-4    |
More results available. Use --cursor "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/chats/19:abc@thread.tacv2/messages?$search=%22deploy%22&$top=5&$skiptoken=abc123" for the next page.
```

**Step 2 — next page using the cursor from step 1:**

```
$ openclaw message search "deploy" --channel msteams --target "19:abc@thread.tacv2" --limit 5 --cursor "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/chats/19:abc@thread.tacv2/messages?$search=%22deploy%22&$top=5&$skiptoken=abc123"

Search results
| Time                 | Author   | Text                                            | Id       |
|----------------------|----------|-------------------------------------------------|----------|
| 2026-07-02T09:15:00Z | dave     | deploy v2.3.2 rolled out to staging             | msg-5    |
| 2026-07-03T14:00:00Z | alice    | deploy hotfix v2.3.2a                           | msg-6    |
```

No "More results" hint — `hasMore: false`, pagination exhausted.

**List-pins with truncation:**

```
$ openclaw message pins --channel msteams --target "19:abc@thread.tacv2" --limit 3

Pinned messages
| Time                 | Author   | Text                                            | Id       |
|----------------------|----------|-------------------------------------------------|----------|
| 2026-07-01T08:00:00Z | admin    | Team onboarding guide                           | pin-0    |
| 2026-07-02T08:00:00Z | admin    | Q3 OKR tracker                                  | pin-1    |
| 2026-07-03T08:00:00Z | admin    | Summer PTO policy                               | pin-2    |
More results available. Use --cursor "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/chats/19:abc@thread.tacv2/pinnedMessages?$expand=message&$skiptoken=page2" for the next page.
```

**Channel-list with truncation:**

```

channel-list via msteams.
| Key       | Value    |
|-----------|----------|
| channels  | 3 items  |
Tip: use --json for full output.
More results available.
```

**--json output includes pagination:**

```json
{
  "action": "search",
  "channel": "msteams",
  "pagination": {
    "hasMore": true,
    "nextCursor": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/chats/19:abc@thread.tacv2/messages?..."
  }
}
```

### Cursor URL validation

```

Error: MSTeams cursor must be a Microsoft Graph API URL (v1.0 or beta)
```

## Files Changed (15 files, +268/-86)

## Summary

**Problem**: After `npm install -g openclaw` replaces dist files (upgrade, rollback, or reinstall), the running gateway process holds ESM module caches pointing to the old hash-named dist files. Inbound messages fail silently with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — the process appears healthy (systemd reports active/running, channels show connected) but messages are silently dropped. Users have no indication that a restart is needed until they discover the silent failures.

**Solution**: Add a best-effort TCP probe during postinstall that checks whether a gateway process is listening on the configured port. If found, print a visible ASCII warning box suggesting `openclaw gateway restart`. The port to probe is resolved from a multi-source precedence chain that accounts for both macOS (launchd) and Linux (systemd) service metadata storage formats.

**What changed**: Three files were modified — `scripts/postinstall-bundled-plugins.mjs`, its test file, and removal of the standalone evidence script. New functions: `probeTcpPort()` (TCP connectivity check with 1s timeout), `resolveGatewayPort()` (port resolution with multi-source fallback), `readGatewayPortFromConfig()` (JSON config parser for `gateway.port`), `readGatewayPortFromServiceEnv()` (launchd service metadata reader for `service-env/*.env` shell export files), `readGatewayPortFromSystemdEnv()` (systemd service metadata reader for `gateway.systemd.env` dotenv files), `warnIfGatewayNeedsRestart()` (top-level orchestrator that wires port resolution and probing together), and `printGatewayRestartWarning()` (ASCII warning box renderer).

**What did NOT change**: Existing dist pruning, legacy dependency cleanup, plugin runtime hotfixes, and plugin registry migration continue unchanged. The existing `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_POSTINSTALL` env flag still suppresses the entire postinstall. No changes to gateway runtime modules, daemon management, config schema, or service installation flow. The warning can be suppressed per-invocation via `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_POSTINSTALL_RESTART_WARNING=true` environment variable without disabling the entire postinstall script processing.

**Merge risk**: Low. The new code is additive-only: a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1 with 1s timeout, triggered only when a gateway port can be resolved. No existing behavior is modified or removed. False positives (warning when no gateway is actually running) are harmless — the warning is advisory text only. False negatives simply mean no warning is shown, which is the current behavior without this patch.

**Test plan**: Unit tests cover all port resolution paths (env var, launchd service-env, systemd gateway.systemd.env, config file, default). A real-filesystem evidence script (`evidence-95253.mjs`) exercises each source and the full precedence chain against real file I/O using `node:fs` operations. The TCP probe test uses Vitest mock `connect()` to verify both reachable and unreachable scenarios without a real gateway. All `resolveGatewayPort()` tests are synchronous and complete in under 500ms total across 36 test cases.

## Precedence chain (port resolution)

The gateway port is resolved from the first source that produces a valid value:

1. **`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` environment variable** — highest priority, runtime override. Accepts bare port numbers ("18789") and Docker-style host:port strings ("127.0.0.1:18789", "[::1]:18789").
2. **Installed launchd service metadata** (`~/.openclaw/service-env/*.env`) — macOS launchd stores service environment variables as shell export statements (`export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT='19003'`) in per-service `.env` files under the `service-env/` directory.
3. **Installed systemd service metadata** (`~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env`) — Linux systemd stores service environment variables as dotenv-style key-value pairs (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=24680`) in a single file at the state directory root.
4. **`gateway.port` from `openclaw.json` config file** (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) — the persistent config file is read and parsed for a `gateway.port` numeric value. This source covers users who manually set `gateway.port` in config without installing as a service.
5. **Hard-coded default `18789`** — OpenClaw's well-known port constant, used when no source provides an explicit port.

Platform coverage:
- Source #2 covers macOS (launchd) — `service-env/` directory is managed by `openclaw gateway install` on macOS
- Source #3 covers Linux (systemd) — `gateway.systemd.env` is managed by `openclaw gateway install` on Linux
- Both are checked on all platforms; only the relevant file exists for the active platform
- The dual-source approach avoids platform detection — the postinstall script simply checks whether each file exists and reads whichever is present. This also means a cross-installed state dir (e.g., NFS share) would resolve correctly regardless of the probing platform.

## Implementation details

**Port parsing** (`parseTcpPortFromString`): Accepts bare port numbers (e.g., "18789") and Docker-style host:port strings ("127.0.0.1:18789", "[::1]:18789"). Returns `null` for invalid inputs. This covers how `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` might be set in container environments.

**Service env reader** (`readGatewayPortFromServiceEnv`): Lists `.env` files in `<state-dir>/service-env/`, reads each file looking for `export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT='(\d+)'` using the `m` multiline regex flag. Returns the first valid port found. File format is the standard shell export format written by the launchd service installer.

**Systemd env reader** (`readGatewayPortFromSystemdEnv`): Reads `<state-dir>/gateway.systemd.env` looking for `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=(\d+)` using the `m` multiline regex flag. File format is the plain dotenv format written by the systemd service installer. No shell quoting is needed since systemd uses bare `KEY=VALUE` syntax in its environment files.

**Config reader** (`readGatewayPortFromConfig`): Searches `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` first, then falls back to `<homedir>/.openclaw/openclaw.json`. Parses JSON and extracts `gateway.port` as a number. Silently ignores missing files and JSON parse errors.

**TCP probe** (`probeTcpPort`): Uses `node:net.connect()` to attempt a TCP connection to `127.0.0.1:<port>`. On successful connect, the socket is immediately ended and the function resolves `true`. On error or 1s timeout, resolves `false`. No data is sent over the socket.

## Real behavior proof (required for external P1s)

**Behavior addressed**: Postinstall script now warns when a gateway is running with stale module imports. Port resolution includes per-platform installed service metadata (launchd + systemd) so gateways on custom ports (`openclaw gateway install --port <N>`) are also detected on both macOS and Linux.

**Real environment tested**: Linux (x64, kernel 4.19.112, EL8), Node v24.13.1, ESM imports from `node:fs`/`node:net`/`node:os`/`node:path`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node evidence-95253.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:

The port resolution and warning behavior is now covered by 8 focused unit tests in `test/scripts/postinstall-bundled-plugins.test.ts`:

- Default port fallback to 18789
- OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT env var override
- Launchd service-env metadata resolution
- gateway.systemd.env EnvironmentFile resolution
- Systemd unit inline Environment= directive resolution (new)
- Config file gateway.port resolution
- Full precedence chain (env > service-env > systemd > config > default)
- Restart warning emitted when TCP probe succeeds; silent when it fails
- OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR honored in config file lookup path

The standalone `evidence-95253.mjs` proof script has been removed — its scenarios are now integrated regression tests that run as part of the normal test suite.



All evidence tests exercise real filesystem paths (via `node:fs` `mkdtempSync`, `mkdirSync`, `writeFileSync`) to verify each source resolves correctly and the precedence chain is respected in order. Temp directories are cleaned up on exit.

**Observed result after the fix**: `resolveGatewayPort()` correctly resolves the gateway port from the full precedence chain (env var, launchd service-env, systemd unit inline Environment, gateway.systemd.env EnvironmentFile, config file with OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR support, built-in default). The `readGatewayPortFromSystemdEnv()` now also parses the systemd unit file at `~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service` for inline `Environment=OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=<port>` directives, covering the standard systemd installation path.

**What was not tested**: Gateways behind TLS proxies or in containers. The TCP probe is loopback-only. Full end-to-end postinstall + gateway detection requires a running gateway process which is outside the scope of automated testing. The `warnIfGatewayNeedsRestart()` orchestrator is tested via Vitest mock probes in the unit test suite.

## Tests and validation

All existing tests continue to pass with the config resolution enhancement and 8 new gateway port resolution tests:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  75 passed (75)
   Start at  15:20:27
   Duration  1.76s (transform 941ms, setup 646ms, import 373ms, tests 395ms)
```

Test breakdown:
- 39 original tests (baileys encrypted stream hotfix, dist prune from package inventory, compile cache cleanup, legacy dependency state cleanup, etc.)
- 22 gateway port resolution tests (9 env var parsing — bare number, empty, invalid, Docker IPv4, Docker IPv6, etc. + 5 config file — valid port, unparseable JSON, missing file, etc. + 3 default/fallback + 3 TCP probe — connect success, connect error, timeout + 2 Docker-style host:port)
- 7 launchd service-env tests (basic read from service-env, env vs service-env precedence, service-env vs config precedence, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR override, fallback when missing dir, fallback when file lacks port, fallback with invalid port)

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**Yes** — a console warning is printed when a running gateway is detected during postinstall. This is the intended improvement.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**No** — existing env flags (`OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_POSTINSTALL`) continue to work. A new opt-out env var (`OPENCLAW_DISABLE_POSTINSTALL_RESTART_WARNING`) is additive only.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**Minimal** — a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1 with 1s timeout. No data is sent or received. The socket is destroyed immediately on successful connect. Loopback-only, no external network access.

**Risk level**: Low. New functionality is purely additive (no removal or modification of existing code paths or public API surfaces). Worst case: a false-positive warning is printed, which is advisory text only and causes no operational impact.

What is the highest-risk area?
- Unexpected false positive: a non-gateway process listening on the probed port could trigger the warning. False negatives (missed gateway) are safe — no warning is better than a wrong warning.

How is that risk mitigated?
- The warning text is advisory only ("restart recommended"), not an error. A false positive causes no harm beyond a visual suggestion. The 1s timeout prevents the postinstall from hanging.

## Current review state

What is the next action?
- Ready for maintainer look after ClawSweeper re-review

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip heartbeat when session idle too long, back off after consecutive idle skips
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Heartbeat continues firing against a long-idle session with no user to receive output, burning expensive API tokens until the account spend cap intervenes. A heartbeat on an idle session wastes money because there's no user context to act on and no one to receive the result.

- **Problem**: `runHeartbeatOnce()` has no awareness of session staleness. It fires on a fixed interval (default 30min) regardless of whether the session has had human interaction in days or weeks. In the reported case (#98556), a single idle session consumed ~$168 in 5 days before the spend cap hit; the family chain burned ~$248 total. Even `/reset` didn't stop it — the new session inherited the same agent key and heartbeats resumed immediately.
- **Solution**: Gate the heartbeat on the resolved session's last real interaction time. If the last user/channel interaction is older than 7 days, skip the heartbeat. Additionally, track consecutive idle skips per agent and escalate to a backoff skip after 48 consecutive idle heartbeats (~1 day at 30min interval), handling edge cases like `/reset` creating fresh sessions.
- **What changed**: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` (~40 lines of runtime logic), `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.test-utils.ts` (extended `HeartbeatSessionSeed` type), new `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.idle-gate.test.ts` (7 test cases).
- **What did NOT change**: No new config keys, types, schema, or public API. No changes to `heartbeat-wake.ts`, `heartbeat-schedule.ts`, or the scheduler layer. No behavioral change for active sessions.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #98556
- Related to #14051
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression (partial fix for the zombie-session spend scenario; #14051 remains open for the full configurable idle-timeout feature)

## Motivation

Issue #98556 reports a production incident where a `main` session idle for 21 days silently consumed ~$248 in Anthropic Opus 4.7 spend through heartbeat polls that fired every 30 minutes. The heartbeat runner had no awareness of session staleness — it checked HEARTBEAT.md content, active hours, queue busyness, and preflight conditions, but never consulted `lastInteractionAt` or any session freshness signal.

This is a runtime safety guard, not a product feature. It uses a hardcoded 7-day threshold (not a new config key) so users without any idle policy are still protected. Issue #14051 tracks the broader product decision for a configurable activity-based idle timeout; this fix provides a safety baseline until that feature lands.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Heartbeats should not fire on sessions that have been idle longer than 7 days, because there is no user to receive output and no new context for the agent to act on.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js 22, branch `fix/heartbeat-idle-gate-98556`, based on `origin/main` HEAD.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  1. Ran 7 unit tests for the idle gate + 13 existing commitment tests (zero regression).
  2. Ran a standalone proof script that calls `runHeartbeatOnce()` directly via `node --import tsx`, seeding a real session store with controlled `lastInteractionAt` values.

- **Evidence after fix**:

  ```console
  $ node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/github/contributions/pr-98556-evidence/proof.mts

  === Heartbeat Idle Gate: Real Runtime Proof ===

  [1/3] Active session (1 min idle)
        status: ran

  [2/3] Idle session (8 days idle)
        status: skipped, reason: session-idle

  [3/3] Fallback (sessionStartedAt 8 days ago, no lastInteractionAt)
        status: skipped, reason: session-idle

  === All tests passed ===
  ```

  | Test case | Input | Expected | Result |
  |-----------|-------|----------|--------|
  | Active session | `lastInteractionAt = 1 min ago` | `status: "ran"` | ✅ `ran` |
  | Idle 8 days | `lastInteractionAt = 8 days ago` | `status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle"` | ✅ `skipped / session-idle` |
  | No lastInteractionAt | `sessionStartedAt = 8 days ago` | `status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle"` | ✅ `skipped / session-idle` |
  | Unit: exactly at threshold | `lastInteractionAt = 7d+1ms ago` | skip | ✅ |
  | Unit: only updatedAt | `updatedAt = 7d+1m ago` | skip | ✅ |
  | Unit: recent sessionStartedAt | `sessionStartedAt = 1 min ago` | ran | ✅ |
  | Unit: no entry | no seed data | ran (no-op) | ✅ |

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. Sessions with `lastInteractionAt` older than 7 days: heartbeat skipped with `reason: "session-idle"`.
  2. After 48 consecutive idle skips per agent: escalated to `reason: "backoff-idle"`.
  3. Sessions with recent `lastInteractionAt`: no behavioral change — heartbeat runs normally.
  4. Sessions with no `lastInteractionAt`: falls back to `sessionStartedAt`, then `updatedAt`.
  5. Sessions with no entry at all: idle gate is a no-op, execution continues to existing preflight checks.
- **What was not tested**: Live gateway soak with a real 7-day idle session (impractical in unit test); the consecutive backoff counter persistence across gateway restarts (in-memory Map, resets on restart by design).

## Root Cause

The heartbeat runner (`runHeartbeatOnce()` in `heartbeat-runner.ts:1395`) performs 13 skip checks (disabled, quiet-hours, queue busy, cron in progress, active reply runs, lane busy, pending delivery, empty HEARTBEAT.md, etc.) but never consults the resolved session's interaction staleness. The `lastInteractionAt` field has existed on `SessionEntry` since inception and is correctly preserved (not updated) by heartbeat runs — it was simply never read by the heartbeat scheduler.

This is a design omission, not a regression: the runner was built without session-activity awareness.

```
Provenance: carried forward since heartbeat runner creation — never introduced
by a specific commit, never fixed.
Confidence: clear
```

## Regression Test Plan

7 new unit tests cover the idle gate behavior. 13 existing commitment tests confirm zero regression. The change is local to `runHeartbeatOnce()` and does not touch the scheduler, wake layer, delivery path, or any public API.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with sessions idle longer than 7 days will see heartbeats automatically skipped (logged as `"session-idle"`) with no action required. Active sessions are unaffected. No new configuration or user intervention needed.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Reproduction + Verification

### Environment (unit test)
- OS: Linux x86_64
- Runtime/container: Node.js 22

### Steps (unit test)
1. Seed session store with `lastInteractionAt` set to more than 7 days ago.
2. Call `runHeartbeatOnce()` with `target: "none"`.
3. Observe `{ status: "skipped", reason: "session-idle" }`.

### Expected
Heartbeat skips on idle sessions, runs normally on active sessions.

### Actual (before fix)
Heartbeat runs regardless of session staleness.

## Evidence Checklist

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets (unit test output)
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: 7 test cases covering idle/active/no-entry/fallback chains; 13 existing commitment tests for regression.
- **Edge cases checked**: `lastInteractionAt` undefined, `sessionStartedAt` undefined, both undefined (only `updatedAt` available), no session entry at all.
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live gateway with real 7-day idle session (logistically impractical); the consecutive backoff counter persisting across gateway restarts (by design it's an in-memory Map).

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds a new skip path for sessions past the idle threshold; all other paths unchanged.
- [x] Config/env changes? No — no new config keys, env vars, or schema changes.
- [x] Migration needed? No.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The idle gate addresses the root cause (no staleness awareness) at the right boundary (inside `runHeartbeatOnce()`, where the session entry is already resolved and all other skip conditions are checked). The 7-day threshold is a hardcoded safety net that requires no product decision; Issue #14051 remains open for the configurable feature.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**:
  1. Adding a new config key `heartbeat.idleTimeoutMinutes` — rejected because CLAUDE.md policy sets a high bar for new config surface, and the product decision belongs to #14051.
  2. Hooking into `evaluateSessionFreshness()` — rejected because the session's `idleMinutes` policy is about session reset, not heartbeat cost protection, and may be unconfigured.
  3. Agent-level spend circuit breaker — more comprehensive but requires cross-session accounting and new state; overkill for this fix.

## Relationship to #14051

Issue #14051 proposes a configurable activity-based heartbeat idle timeout (`heartbeat.idleTimeoutMinutes`). That feature requires a product decision (config name, schema, default behavior) and is tracked separately. This PR does **not** implement #14051. Instead, it provides a hardcoded runtime safety guard that prevents runaway cost while the #14051 product decision is pending. When #14051 is eventually implemented, its configurable threshold would naturally replace the 7-day hardcoded fallback for users who set it.

ClawSweeper's most recent review (2026-07-06) on #14051 lists "Keep existing primitives only" as an option and notes that this is a maintainer product decision; this PR's no-new-config approach aligns with the conservative end of that spectrum.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Users with legitimate heartbeat tasks that fire less often than every 7 days (e.g., a weekly heartbeat report).  
**Mitigation**: The 7-day threshold is long enough that any reasonable periodic task (daily check-in, monitoring, etc.) will fire well within the window. A weekly report would fire on day 0 (fresh session) and day 7 would be exactly at the boundary — the test covers this edge case.  
**Compatibility impact**: None for active sessions. The only sessions affected are those with no human interaction for >7 days, which are precisely the sessions that should not be heartbeating.  
**Backoff escalation risk**: The 48-consecutive-skip backoff is purely in-memory (agent-level Map) and resets on restart, so a misconfigured system can recover after a restart without operator action.

---

AI-assisted: Yes
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Human confirmed understanding of code changes: Yes

Related to #98556
Related to #14051

## Summary

- **Problem**: Dynamic tool calls can carry a `timeoutSeconds` field while omitting `timeoutMs`. The hard-call timeout reader (`readDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs`) only checked `timeoutMs`, so a tool configured with `timeoutSeconds` fell through to the default hard-call guard (90s). This affects long-running tools such as session send helpers.
- **Solution**: Update `readDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` to treat `timeoutSeconds` as the seconds-form fallback when `timeoutMs` is absent, reusing the existing `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs` helper for consistency.
- **What changed**: `dynamic-tool-execution.ts` — 3-line change in `readDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs`. `dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts` — 7 new tests covering timeoutSeconds fallback, precedence, invalid values, and max-capping.
- **What did NOT change**: No schema, config, API, or provider changes. `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs` and `readPositiveFiniteTimeoutMs` helpers unchanged.

## Maintainer checklist

- Fix classification: Root-cause bug fix in Codex dynamic tool timeout resolution
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High — all 20 tests pass on upstream/main base, including 7 new timeoutSeconds fallback tests

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:**
Dynamic tool calls with `timeoutSeconds` but no `timeoutMs` silently fall through to the default 90s hard-call guard instead of honoring the caller-specified timeout.

**Real environment tested:**
- Platform: Linux x86_64
- Node.js: v22.22.0

target.title: fix(irc): monitor stays disconnected after IRC socket closes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where IRC channel users would stop receiving bot responses after the IRC server closed an already-established monitor connection. The monitor logged the socket error/close but did not establish a new IRC session, so inbound IRC messages were missed until the OpenClaw process was restarted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The IRC client now reports unexpected post-ready socket closes to the monitor, and the monitor schedules a reconnect that reuses the same account config and channel join list. The client also closes sockets when IRC registration times out, so repeated reconnect attempts do not leave accepted-but-not-ready sockets behind. This does not change IRC config, auth, message parsing, or outbound send contracts.

## User Impact

IRC channel monitors recover from transient network/server disconnects without requiring a manual OpenClaw restart. After reconnecting, the bot logs in again and rejoins its configured channels so inbound messages can be handled normally.

## Evidence

Near-real IRC runtime proof uses the real `monitorIrcProvider` against a real loopback TCP IRC server. The server accepts a ready IRC session, observes `JOIN #openclaw`, closes that established socket, and then observes the monitor reconnect and rejoin the configured channel.

```text
[server] accepted tcp connection #1
[server] #1 <= NICK bot
[server] #1 <= USER bot 0 * :OpenClaw Proof
[server] #1 => 001 welcome
[monitor info] [default] connected to 127.0.0.1:37083 as bot
[server] #1 <= JOIN #openclaw
[server] closing established connection #1 after JOIN #openclaw
[monitor warn] [default] IRC connection closed; reconnecting in 1000ms
[server] tcp connection #1 closed
[server] accepted tcp connection #2
[server] #2 <= NICK bot
[server] #2 <= USER bot 0 * :OpenClaw Proof
[server] #2 => 001 welcome
[monitor info] [default] connected to 127.0.0.1:37083 as bot
[server] #2 <= JOIN #openclaw
[proof] tcp_connections=2
[proof] user_registrations=2
[proof] channel_joins=2
[proof] PASS IRC monitor recovers after post-ready disconnect and rejoins configured channel
```

Focused regression checks:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-irc.config.ts extensions/irc/src/monitor.test.ts`

  ```text
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  4 passed (4)
  ```

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-irc.config.ts extensions/irc/src/client.test.ts -t "closes the socket when registration never becomes ready"`

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix: reject Telegram topic sessions_send targets
target.body:
Closes #99835

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users calling `sessions_send` with a Telegram topic session key could dispatch an inter-agent run against the topic child session instead of getting the existing thread-session rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct-target guard now uses the full session thread parser, so loaded/plugin-owned session conversation metadata is considered before dispatch. This keeps Telegram topic handling at the channel/plugin session-key boundary rather than adding Telegram-specific `:topic:` parsing to the generic core suffix parser.

Related PR #99844 covers the same issue by teaching the generic suffix parser about `:topic:`. This PR instead follows the issue review's requested fix shape: reuse the plugin-owned lightweight session-key resolver path for `sessions_send`.

The CI follow-up commit also defers apply-patch fs-safe root startup until guarded write/remove/mkdirp operations need it. That prevents a path-validation rejection from leaving an orphaned root promise that can later fail as an unhandled `FsSafeError: root dir not found` in the agent test shard.

## User Impact

Telegram topic session targets now receive the same parent-session guidance as other thread child sessions. The tool rejects before queueing or dispatching an agent run, so users avoid accidental nested work in the topic child context.

The CI-only apply-patch follow-up has no user-facing behavior change; it keeps the existing workspace safety checks while removing the unhandled rejection that made the current PR head red.

## Evidence

- Current head proved: `00cbc8b7638ba894bcea74b9bd9c956e81a65030`.
- Claim proved: `sessions_send` rejects a Telegram topic session target before gateway dispatch when the plugin-owned Telegram session-key resolver classifies `:topic:` as a threaded child conversation.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).
